searchText: <@!539495253418180618> Note that there is probably a large diff in speed between the GMP and LLVM backend. Also for our usecase at Nimbus, the secret sauce (Xbyak JIT) does not work on ARM. I didn't benchmark Milagro yet but this is mcl on Raspberry Pi 4 (relevant ops are pairing for verification and scalar multiplication for key generation and signing: https://github.com/mratsim/mcl/blob/bench-arm32-pi4/bench-arm32-pi4.log) not that it was compiled in 32-bit mode the hashToG2 was the old version. The new version based on the IETF draft is probably slower as there are some HKDF rounds and some isogeny-based cryptography mixed in I wonder how a handwritten native llvm ir version would fare ie one that uses the llvm big int support There was a huge PR with **293** commits that was merged into the hash-to-curve repo this weekend. https://github.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-hash-to-curve/pull/208/files Any idea if this is a fundamental change? From a quick glance it looks cosmetic (hash2curve -> hash_to_curve, or map2base -> map_to_base) and it seems like it was the version that was already uploaded on the IETF website but who knows
